data.narrative:
Cellcolabs is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Mattias Bernow that has raised $37M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private companies including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Chai Discovery.

Only one valuation method proved applicable given data constraints. Stage-progression analysis uses the $37M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $74M. The peer-median approach cannot be applied: while 8 same-sector private comparables exist, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, similar-tier) produced fewer than the required 3 datapoints. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable because target revenue is not disclosed, precluding use of the sector P/S median of 5.6x observed across the three public peers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $63M to $85M, with $74M as the central estimate. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression method. Key uncertainties limiting precision include the absence of revenue data for revenue-multiple calibration and the insufficient density of directly comparable private peers at identical stage and valuation tier. Resolution of revenue or customer metrics would enable public-comp triangulation and materially tighten the range.
